content.text:
I searched CPRD and found only two Read codes that specifically mean hidradenitis suppurativa (HS).

**Hidradenitis suppurativa codelist**

| Read code | Term | Notes |
|:--|:--|:--|
| M25y1 | Hidradenitis | Parent code. In Read coding, this is the code used for HS. |
| M25y1-1 | Hidradenitis suppurativa | Synonym of M25y1. |

**Searches I ran:**
- **Words:** "hidradenitis", "hydradenitis", "suppurativa", "acne inversa", "Verneuil", "follicular occlusion", "apocrine" and "sweat gland abscess". The last two only found codes for other conditions; the rest found HS or nothing.
- **Code branches:** M25y (other sweat gland disorders) and M253.

**Codes I left out because they're too broad or a different condition:**
- **Too general:** M25y (Other specified sweat gland disorders), M25yz (Other sweat gland disorder NOS), M25yX (Apocrine sweat disorder, unspecified), Myu6D ([X]Other apocrine sweat disorders) and Myu6J (Disorder of apocrine gland). Some HS cases may sit under these, but adding them would bring in other conditions. You could include them in a separate sensitivity analysis.
- **Different conditions:** Fox-Fordyce disease (M25y0), Bromhidrosis (M25y2), Chromhidrosis (M25y3), Granulosis rubra nasi (M25y4) and Acne keloid (M25y6).

Some HS may be recorded under general codes for skin abscess, boils or pilonidal disease instead of the HS code. Those codes can't reliably identify HS, so I didn't include them.

content.text:
CPRD has only two Read codes that mean hidradenitis suppurativa, so the codelist is short.

**Hidradenitis suppurativa codelist (CPRD)**

| Read code | Term | Include |
|---|---|---|
| M25y1 | Hidradenitis | Yes |
| M25y1-1 | Hidradenitis suppurativa | Yes |

**Codes I found but left out (you may want to look at these):**

| Read code | Term | Why it's left out |
|---|---|---|
| 7G030 | Excision of sweat gland-bearing skin of axilla | Surgery that's often done for hidradenitis suppurativa, but also for excessive sweating (hyperhidrosis). It's only an optional sign of the condition. |
| 7G031 | Excision of sweat gland bearing skin of groin | Same as above |
| 7G032 | Excision of sweat gland bearing skin | Same as above |
| 7C160 / 7D076 | Excision of sweat gland bearing skin of male / female perineum | Same as above |
| 7G03E | Subcutaneous excision of sweat gland tissue of axilla | Mostly done for excessive sweating |
| M25yX | Apocrine sweat disorder, unspecified | Too vague |
| Myu6D | [X]Other apocrine sweat disorders | Too vague |
| Myu6J | Disorder of apocrine gland | Too vague |
| M25, M25y, M25yz, M25z | General or "other" sweat gland disorder codes | Too vague |
| M25y0 | Fox-Fordyce disease | A different condition |

**How I searched:** I searched the terms "hidradenitis", "hydradenitis", "acne inversa", "Verneuil", "apocrine", "sweat gland" and "sweat gland abscess". I also searched the code families M25y and M253. Only the two codes in the main table refer specifically to the condition.

If you want to find more cases, you could add the sweat gland skin excision codes (7G030–7G032, 7C160, 7D076). They'll mainly catch people having surgery for hidradenitis suppurativa, but some will be people treated for excessive sweating, so expect some wrong matches.
